messages:
Alex: heads up — during the canary today we saw quota spikes for the new edge route when we switched it to protobuf-over-http. looks like quota keys aren't lining up with the legacy REST path
Maria: ugh, that sounds like header propagation or route key naming. which limiter are we hitting?
Alex: per-tenant rate limiter. quota dashboard shows tenant X getting charged on both /v1/generate (rest) and /rpc.Generate (grpc) separately, so double-counting in the console.
Sasha: double-counting? can you paste the raw request headers? maybe x-tenant-id vs x-tenant?
Alex: pasted below (redacted):
```
:method: POST
:authority: api.redwood.internal
:path: /rpc.Generate
content-type: application/grpc+proto
x-tenant-id: tenant-x
x-route-id: edge-gen-blue
```
Maria: compare that to the REST request header we used previously — our limiter keys were computed from path + tenant header, but the gateway canonicalizer maps gRPC methods to service/method names and we didn't update the limiter key function.
Jordan: so gateway canonicalization changed the route id from '/v1/generate' to 'rpc.Generate' and the quota key hash is different -> cost shows up under a new metric.
OpsRun: deploy-bot triggered canary roll 2028-11-03T15:21:02Z :rocket: (note: small traffic percentage)
Sasha: two problems: billing/console UX (different metric labels) and enforcement (we're not deduping the hit). enforcement probably sees them as distinct tokens and lets both through.
Alex: observed a brief window where a client retried and both REST fallback and gRPC attempt counted separately. end-user saw doubled usage.
Maria: proposal: implement a thin policy-adapter in gateway that emits a normalized route tag used both by limiters and metrics. mapping rules can be additive so we can support both shapes.
Jordan: +1. keep mapping table in control-plane so Console shows a single logical route for quota. also expose a mapping preview in Console for rollouts.
Sasha: suggestion: mapping rules should be declarative and versioned. e.g.
```
- name: generate
  canonical: /v1/generate
  aliases: ["rpc.Generate", "/internal/generate"]
  ttl: 1h
```
Maria: and add a canary mode where both raw and canonical metrics are emitted for 24h so we can validate no regressions in counting.
Alex: ops note: we need fallback for legacy tenants that rely on 'x-tenant' header vs 'x-tenant-id', so adapter should support header aliases too.
OpsRun: created ticket INF-2931 to track policy-adapter work and console mapping UX, assigned to @Maria and @Jordan.
Jordan: for enforcement: change limiter key derivation to prefer canonical route then fall back to raw path. low-risk flag rollout.
Sasha: telemetry: add a metric "route_canonicalization_mismatch" to surface how often alias used vs canonical. gradient alert if mismatch > 5% during rollout.
Alex: can we get a console preview that shows projected quota delta when mapping applied? would help support and billing.
Maria: yeah—Console team: we can add a table: alias -> canonical -> delta_estimate. need backend endpoint that returns delta for a candidate mapping over a sliding 24h window.
Jordan: implementation plan: 1) gateway adapter (control-plane mappings) 2) limiter key change behind feature flag 3) telemetry metric + alert 4) Console preview + canary release 5) roll mapping to default after 48h stable.
Sasha: small implementation detail: when canonicalizing gRPC, strip method args and keep only service.method, normalized to lower-case to avoid casing mismatch.
Alex: I'll run a short load test post-PR to validate dedupe. can everyone review the INF-2931 checklist?
Maria: reviewing now. grateful for the canary telemetry callouts — avoids billing surprises. :+1:
Jordan: ping me on the PR and I'll coordinate the feature-flag rollout window.
deploy-bot: build/4521 succeeded for gateway-policy-adapter (sha: b3f4a2) — staging deploy queued.
Alex: nice, staging smoke next. I'll try the retry pattern and confirm counters are stable.
Sasha: keep traces — add a tag canonical_route to span so tracing shows mapping decisions.
OpsRun: noted. adding tracing task to INF-2931.
Maria: ok wrapping up, next sync in #eng-platform tomorrow 10:30am to review telemetry after staging run.
Jordan: thanks all — this pattern will be useful for other protocol translations too.
Alex: thanks!
